messages:
Aditi R.: FYI ran a 30s perf sample on a 2k-token batch to repro the noisy canary latency. Looks like CPU-side overhead, not GPU stall.
Samir G.: can you paste the exact perf commands and a short list of top stacks? wondering if batcher locks or tokenizer are to blame
Aditi R.: recorded with:
```
pid=$(pgrep -f 'redwood-runtime')\nperf record -F 99 -g -p $pid -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 30\nperf script /tmp/perf.data | stackcollapse-perf.pl > /tmp/out.folded\n./flamegraph.pl /tmp/out.folded > /tmp/sampler.svg\n```
Top collapsed stacks I pulled out:
- runtime.scheduler::acquire_batch_lock -> Scheduler.spin_wait -> PyThread_acquire_lock
- tokenizer._fast_tokenize -> re.sub -> PyUnicode_Find
- http.request::parse_headers -> urllib3.connectionpool
Jun Park: spin_wait + PyThread_acquire_lock suggests frequent thread wakeups. Could be batcher notify()s w/ tiny per-request work. Can you run `perf sched record` and share wakeup chains?
Aditi R.: did that. sched trace shows many short wakeups:
```
batcher_dispatcher -> pthread_cond_signal -> worker_thread wakeup -> GIL acquire -> tokenize -> yield -> wait
```
So lots of GIL churn for small tokenize work.
Maya L.: what's the canary batcher config? max_batch_ms / max_tokens / concurrency?
Aditi R.: canary: max_batch_ms=3, max_tokens=2048, concurrency=16. We lowered max_batch_ms for latency, but looks like we're paying in context switches and scheduler time.
Samir G.: two quick experiments: 1) raise max_batch_ms to 8 on staging and re-run perf; 2) add histograms: tokens_per_batch and wakeups_per_batch to batcher metrics.
Jun Park: also consider moving hot tokenization into a tiny Cython function to avoid repeated PyUnicode_Find calls, or add prefix-KV cache to skip tokenize on repeated prefixes.
Aditi R.: did a fast A/B: bumped max_batch_ms to 8 and re-sampled. Results: ~35% fewer context switches, scheduler CPU down, but small-request tail increased ~+8ms. Overall throughput improved and tail tradeoff seems reasonable.
perf-ci-bot: artifacts uploaded https://ci.internal.redwood/runs/98765/artifacts/sampler.svg :eyes:
Maya L.: paste top stacks as text for the run after change so we can put in the doc (some folks can't open SVGs)
Aditi R.: top 3 stacks after bump (text):
1) runtime.kv_cache::lookup -> memchr
2) runtime.scheduler::dispatch_batch -> pthread_cond_wait
3) tokenizer._fast_tokenize -> re.sub
Tokenizer reduced; pthread_cond_wait increased relatively (fewer wakeups, longer batching).
Samir G.: regression checklist we should collect before any rollout: perf(99Hz) before/after, perf sched traces (wakeup chains), histograms tokens_per_batch & wakeups_per_batch, microbench tokenizer python vs cython. Also capture kernel and python build info for perf reproducibility.
Maya L.: i'll add a feature flag that sets default max_batch_ms=8 and exposes the histograms on /metrics/batcher. Default for latency-sensitive tenants will remain at 3ms until they opt-in.
Aditi R.: plan: ship flag to staging, run overnight 1M-token steady-state load, collect perf+perf sched+histograms. If 99p latency stable, promote to canary. I'll also attach /proc/version and `python -V` to artifacts.
Jun Park: i'll spike a Cython tokenizer today; if it's a small win we can gate it behind a build-time flag and fallback to pure Python for private builds.
Maya L.: backlog task: prefix-kvcache spike + perf delta.
Aditi R.: also adding a short patch that logs wakeups_per_batch to debug logs for one replica so we can correlate request ids to wakeup spikes.
Samir G.: ack, tag me when artifacts are uploaded.
perf-ci-bot: build queued for branch/batcher-opt (run 4321)
Maya L.: small reminder: include a rollback toggle and keep old defaults for customers that opt into ultra-low p50.
Aditi R.: noted, thanks all :thumbsup:
